title: Glucose test in pregnancy
what: You give blood on an empty stomach, drink a sweet glucose solution, and give blood again after one hour and after two. This checks how your body handles sugar.
why: Usually at 24 to 28 weeks of pregnancy, to catch gestational diabetes in time. Sometimes earlier, if your doctor sees a reason.
duration: about 2 to 2.5 hours; results usually come in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If your blood sugar was high before
If you have a cold or feel unwell right now

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Fasting: usually 8 to 14 hours without food. Plain water is fine.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Eat as usual. Do not diet in the days before. In the evening, do not overeat sweets.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor how to take your morning medicines.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Keep your morning free. You need to sit quietly at the clinic for 2 hours.

bring: Water and a snack for after the test
A book or something to pass the time
steps: In the morning, on an empty stomach, blood is taken from a vein
You drink a glass of sweet solution within 5 minutes
You sit quietly. No walking, eating, or drinking
After one hour, blood is taken a second time
After two hours, a third time
feel: The solution is very sweet and may make you feel sick
Sometimes mild weakness or dizziness. Tell the nurse
Three needle pricks in the vein
after: Results usually come in 1 to 2 days. Your doctor will explain them
If your sugar is high, your doctor will talk about diet and monitoring

faq.q: Why can't I walk around during the test?
faq.a: Movement burns sugar and skews the result. You need to sit quietly.

faq.q: What if I throw up the drink?
faq.a: Tell the nurse. Usually the test is stopped and moved to another day.

faq.q: Is the glucose harmful to my baby?
faq.a: No. It is a normal amount of sugar, like in a sweet drink.

reminders.text: Glucose test tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Water is fine. No breakfast and nothing sweet in the morning.
